subject.title: [Feature]: Inbound media shared across all agents — no per-agent isolation

question: What identity should OpenClaw use as the durable inbound-media isolation boundary across save, resolve, stage, cleanup, and plugin APIs?
rationale: The current evidence proves the flat media pool remains, but choosing account, resolved agent, session, channel/chat, tenant, or an indexed provenance model is a security and compatibility decision automation should not invent.

options.title: Adopt managed scoped media contract
options.body: Define a core contract for scoped managed inbound media, then update bundled channels, resolvers, staging, cleanup, docs, and tests together.

options.title: Limit scope to account subdirs
options.body: Use sanitized channel/account identifiers as the first isolation step, accepting that session/chat/tenant provenance remains separate follow-up work.

options.title: Defer until media provenance design
options.body: Keep this tracker open but wait for a broader media-index or provenance schema decision before changing the filesystem layout.

recommendation.title: Adopt managed scoped media contract
recommendation.body: Define a core contract for scoped managed inbound media, then update bundled channels, resolvers, staging, cleanup, docs, and tests together.

likelyOwner.reason: The current history routes the central media-reference, media-store, and staging decisions through this area owner most strongly.
